summary: `phasekit upgrade` now commits the files it wrote (chore(scaffold): phasekit upgrade vX.Y.Z -> vA.B.C) and pushes when the branch has an upstream, leaving the tree clean. Opt out with --no-commit. Only the paths the upgrade touched are committed, via `git commit --only`, so a project's in-flight work is never swept into a scaffold commit. Every git failure is non-fatal.
suggested_commit_message: session lifetime: phasekit upgrade commits and pushes its own work
reviewer_notes: REAL BUG CAUGHT BY A TEST I WROTE FOR THE SHARP EDGE. The first implementation staged the touched paths then ran a plain `git commit`, which commits the WHOLE index — so a change the project had already staged when the upgrade ran was swept into a commit whose message says 'phasekit upgrade'. That is worse than the dirty tree being fixed: it gives someone's in-flight work the wrong story and hides it in a scaffold commit. Fixed with `git commit --only -- <paths>`, which commits exactly those paths and leaves the rest of the index staged.

Test-side over-assertion corrected honestly rather than by weakening the feature: .scaffold/manifest.json is only committed WHEN IT CHANGES. A re-upgrade at the same scaffold version regenerates a byte-identical manifest, and committing that would be exactly the empty-commit churn the idempotence test forbids. The test now drops the manifest from the index first so the assertion means something.
Push is attempted only when a remote AND an upstream exist. A standalone project with neither is the normal public case, not a failure — it prints a note and keeps the commit local.

Non-fatal throughout, including no git identity: the files are already installed on disk by the time the commit is attempted, so turning a git-config problem into an upgrade failure would be strictly worse. Pinned by a test that unsets user.email/user.name and asserts the upgrade still exits 0 with the file present.
Documented in docs/INSTALL_LIFECYCLE.md with both failure modes that motivated it, so the next person does not read this as gratuitous git automation.
